Modified assessment incorporating Beige Book insights

- Policy stance: The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continued balance sheet runoff, keeping policy restrictive while inflation has eased but remains elevated. Guidance highlights that tighter financial and credit conditions will weigh on activity and hiring.
- Beige Book corroboration (New York District references): Reports indicate easing labor demand, softer consumer spending, moderating inflationary pressures, and weak housing markets, with inventories generally manageable. These observations are consistent with slowing aggregate activity and cooling price momentum noted by the Committee.
- Credit conditions: SLOOS shows tighter standards and weaker demand across C&I, CRE, and consumer credit, with approvals more sensitive to borrower quality; CRE collateral concerns remain elevated. This implies persistent credit restraint.
- Risk balance: While the banking system is resilient, vulnerabilities (especially CRE and nonbank finance) persist. Combined with Beige Book evidence of softer demand, risks are skewed to the downside for growth even as inflation pressures ease.

Net effect on tone: Slightly more negative than a mildly negative baseline given corroborating Beige Book softness and ongoing credit tightening.
